newsitem.title: INDIA: India VSNL finalises GDR issue syndicate.
newsitem.headline: India VSNL finalises GDR issue syndicate.

text.p: India's state-run overseas telecommunications monopoly Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) said on Friday it had finalised an international syndicate for its proposed issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs).
VSNL's GDR issue has been put off several times since 1994 because of adverse market conditions and bureaucratic delays, analysts said.

"VSNL, the ministry of finance, the department of telecommunications, SBI Capital Markets and the joint global coordinators -- Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, Jardine Fleming and Salomon Brothers -- today confirmed the international syndicate structure and members for the offering of global depositary receipts by VSNL," the firm said in a statement.

Cazenove & Co, HSBC James Capel, Merrill Lynch, and Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) would be the co-lead managers, it said. BZW, CS First Boston, ING Barings, Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley and Peregrine would be co-managers, it added.
SBI Capital Markets will be the domestic advisor to the company for the issue, VSNL said.
"The GDRs will be marketed to investors around the world through a global syndicate. VSNL confirms the invitation to foreign banks to participate in the international syndicate," the statement said.
"The issue is likely to take place in the first quarter of 1997," a spokesman for VSNL told Reuters.
Market sources have earlier estimated that the issue, the third launch attempt in two years after two unsuccesful attempts in 1994, will be between $650 million and $800 million.

"The international syndicate and team of advisors has been selected to reflect the anticipated scale of this flagship GDR issue," the statement quoted VSNL chairman and managing director B.K. Syngal as saying.

"The syndicate has been broadbased and designed to ensure the most comprehensive coverage of the international investment community, providing combined strengths in distribution, research and trading," he said.
